title: Edge-localized modes and MHD stability control
bottleneck: High-performance tokamak plasmas suffer edge-localized modes, periodic eruptions that eject energy bursts capable of eroding divertor surfaces in a power plant. Suppressing ELMs with resonant magnetic perturbations or pellet pacing works on current machines but can degrade core confinement or prove incompatible with burning-plasma conditions. Uncontrolled ELMs at reactor scale would destroy plasma-facing components within months.
why_it_blocks: ELM control is a make-or-break issue for the tokamak power-plant path. The operating regimes with the best fusion performance are also the ones most threatened by ELMs.
current_state: ELM suppression has been demonstrated on DIII-D, KSTAR, and others. Whether these techniques survive in self-heated burning plasmas with alpha-particle effects is unknown. ITER plans to test ELM control coils at near-reactor scale, but results will not arrive until the 2030s.
